newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares start thin bourse slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares start thin bourse slightly lower.

text.p: German shares began thin bourse trade lower on Monday, coming off record highs, as the dollar's weakness against the mark pulled the market down.
The dollar had fallen sharply under 1.51 marks on Friday and dollar weakness is seen as negative for German exporters.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares started floor dealings down at 2,729.59 points, later recovering somewhat to stand off 3.38 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2,736.45, just below its record close of 2,739.83 reached on Friday.

With support coming from a firm Friday close on Wall Street and a stronger German government bond market, dealers did not want to rule out the possibility that the index could test record high levels reached on Friday.

Chemicals group BASF AG fell 34 pfennigs to 51.40 marks, despite the company saying the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it conditional approval to market its Meridia TM obesity drug in the U.S..

Drugs group Schering also lost ground, falling 35 pfennigs to 123.90 marks, although the firm announced positive nine-month figures. Schering said nine month profits were 286 million marks compared with 172 million marks in the previous year.

One of the morning's biggest gainers was dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, which rose over five percent, up 6.90 marks to 143 marks, recovering losses made on Friday when the firm released nine month results. The stock had climbed in New York.

Meanwhile, state-owned telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, part of which is due to be floated next week, said it had topped up the volume of its share issue to 600 million shares or three billion marks from 500 million shares or 2.5 billion marks.
Dealers said the news had pushed down the price of Telekom shares in "grey" or unofficial pre-flotation telephone dealings, to 33.00 to 33.50 marks, from 34 marks.
Shares in the world's largest reinsurance group, Munich Re (Muenchener Rueckversichering) were down 45 marks at 3,750 marks after the firm announced results for the 1995/96 financial year.
